heritage.name: Taj Mahal
heritage.description: The Taj Mahal is a monumental mausoleum complex in Agra, built during the Mughal period and renowned for its architecture, marble work and gardens.
heritage.historicalSignificance: It is one of the best-known monuments associated with Mughal architecture and the cultural history of India.
heritage.architecture: Mughal architecture with Persian, Central Asian and Indian influences.

heritage.name: Red Fort
heritage.description: The Red Fort is a major historic fort complex in Delhi constructed under the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.
heritage.historicalSignificance: The fort was a major political and ceremonial center of the Mughal Empire and later became an important symbol of modern India.
heritage.architecture: Mughal architecture featuring red sandstone structures, gardens, halls and decorative work.

heritage.name: Qutb Minar
heritage.description: Qutb Minar is a monumental minaret complex in Delhi associated with the early Delhi Sultanate.
heritage.historicalSignificance: The complex preserves important evidence of medieval architecture and the early Delhi Sultanate period.
heritage.architecture: Indo-Islamic architecture using sandstone and carved decorative elements.

heritage.name: Ajanta Caves
heritage.description: Ajanta is a group of rock-cut Buddhist caves famous for murals, sculptures and monastic architecture.
heritage.historicalSignificance: The caves provide important evidence of ancient Indian Buddhist art, architecture and religious life.

heritage.name: Ellora Caves
heritage.description: Ellora is a large complex of rock-cut monuments representing Buddhist, Hindu and Jain traditions.
heritage.historicalSignificance: The caves demonstrate the coexistence of different religious and artistic traditions in historical India.
heritage.architecture: Rock-cut architecture including temples, monasteries and sculptural complexes.

heritage.name: Group of Monuments at Hampi
heritage.description: Hampi contains the remains of the historic capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.
heritage.historicalSignificance: The monuments reveal the political, economic, religious and artistic importance of the Vijayanagara Empire.
heritage.architecture: South Indian temple and imperial architecture.

heritage.name: Great Wall of China
heritage.description: The Great Wall is a vast system of fortifications constructed and expanded by successive Chinese states and dynasties.
heritage.historicalSignificance: It represents centuries of military, political and engineering history in China.
heritage.architecture: Walls, watchtowers, gates and defensive structures.

heritage.name: Forbidden City
heritage.description: The Forbidden City is a vast imperial palace complex in Beijing that served as the center of Chinese imperial government for centuries.
heritage.historicalSignificance: It preserves the architectural and political heritage of China's imperial dynasties.

heritage.name: Terracotta Army
heritage.description: The Terracotta Army is a large collection of life-size clay military figures associated with the mausoleum of Qin Shi Huang.
heritage.historicalSignificance: The figures provide important evidence about Qin military organization, craftsmanship and funerary practices.
heritage.architecture: Underground burial pits and monumental mausoleum complex.

heritage.name: Colosseum
heritage.description: The Colosseum is a monumental Roman amphitheatre in the center of Rome.
heritage.historicalSignificance: It is one of the most important surviving monuments of Roman imperial architecture and public entertainment.
heritage.architecture: Roman amphitheatre architecture using arches, vaults and multiple levels.

heritage.name: Pompeii
heritage.description: Pompeii is an ancient Roman city preserved by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE.
heritage.historicalSignificance: The site provides an unusually detailed view of everyday Roman urban life.
heritage.architecture: Roman streets, houses, temples, baths, theatres and public buildings.

heritage.name: Stonehenge
heritage.description: Stonehenge is a prehistoric monument consisting of large stones arranged in a distinctive ceremonial landscape.
heritage.historicalSignificance: It provides evidence of complex prehistoric construction, ceremonial activity and social organization.

heritage.name: Tower of London
heritage.description: The Tower of London is a historic castle complex founded after the Norman Conquest.
heritage.historicalSignificance: The Tower served as a royal palace, fortress, prison, treasury and important political site.
heritage.architecture: Norman and later medieval fortress architecture.

heritage.name: Alhambra
heritage.description: The Alhambra is a historic palace and fortress complex associated with the Nasrid dynasty of Granada.
heritage.historicalSignificance: It is one of the most significant surviving examples of medieval Islamic architecture in the Iberian Peninsula.
heritage.architecture: Islamic palace architecture featuring courtyards, gardens, geometric decoration and water features.

heritage.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
heritage.description: Mont-Saint-Michel is a historic tidal island and abbey complex on the Normandy coast.
heritage.historicalSignificance: It became an important medieval religious and pilgrimage center.

heritage.name: Acropolis of Athens
heritage.description: The Acropolis is an ancient fortified hill containing major monuments of Classical Greek architecture.
heritage.historicalSignificance: It represents the architectural, artistic and cultural achievements of Classical Athens.

heritage.name: Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto
heritage.description: The historic monuments of Kyoto include temples, shrines, gardens and other structures reflecting Japanese cultural history.
heritage.historicalSignificance: Kyoto was a major political, religious and cultural center of Japan for centuries.
heritage.architecture: Traditional Japanese temple, shrine and garden architecture.

heritage.name: Uluru
heritage.description: Uluru is a massive sandstone formation with deep cultural significance to the Anangu people.
heritage.historicalSignificance: The site is an important part of Indigenous Australian cultural traditions and landscape knowledge.
heritage.architecture: Natural geological formation rather than built architecture.
